Population increased in North Yorkshire

The estimated population of North Yorkshire in 2024 was 635,270 usual residents, a rise of 1.0% since 2023.

This meant that North Yorkshire's rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of North Yorkshire increased by 2.7%.

Over this slightly longer period, North Yorkshire was also among the areas that had a broadly average population increase, of local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of North Yorkshire

The average (median) age fell to 48.7 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of North Yorkshire has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
North Yorkshire is an area that is classed as rural in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, North Yorkshire's population of 635,270 usual residents was made up of:

  • 100,546 people aged 0 to 15 years, (15.8%)
  • 369,521 people aged 16 to 64 years, (58.2%)
  • 165,203 people aged 65 years and over, (26%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, North Yorkshire has a higher proportion of people aged 65 years and over (26% compared with 18.9% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In North Yorkshire, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net internal migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in North Yorkshire
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for North Yorkshire, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More deaths than births led to a fall in the population of 2,341 people (-0.4%). In total, there were 4,753 births and 7,094 deaths in North Yorkshire.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) increased the population by 5,363 (0.9%). There were 30,994 people entering the area and 25,631 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in North Yorkshire's population of 3,132 (0.5%) as a result of 4,863 people entering the area and 1,731 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for North Yorkshire was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of North Yorkshire in mid-2023 is 628,846.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 1,415 people and internal migration estimates were revised downwards by 198 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 1,217 people.
